title: Equipment Performance System
promise: Lost hours stop being an opinion.

hero.h1: Lost hours stop being an opinion. Every one has a name.
hero.dek: One database for the whole plant. The line's own run signal and its own counters are worked out once, on the server — and every lost hour walks back to a minute, a machine and a person's word about what happened.

Correct it where it was declared and every total that used it corrects itself, back through the history.

The run signal is the one the SCADA already shows on the operator's page, and TimeLens replays that same page from the historian at any moment you name. The number, the screen and the recording are one plant record.

sections.title: Stops and the reason
Asked once, at the restart, in two taps.

screen.chrome: EPS · Beverage Line 7 · the restart card
screen.caption: the card that opens by itself when the line comes back: which side did it come from, then the machine

items.lead: The card that opens at the restart
items.text: The line comes back, the operator has just cleared the cause, and the card is already open — named in two taps.
Tap one, then Record: the stop leaves the list, named, with who said so and when.
More reasons, then the side it came from, then the machine, the kind and the cause — the loss is filed against the machine that caused it, not the one that stopped.
Type it in the box and record it as other: an honest record of a stop nobody can name, instead of a wrong reason on the sheet.
The operator still firefighting presses Later: the stop waits in the backlog, nothing is written, and nobody is told he looked.

items.lead: Small stops are never a popup
items.text: A stop too short for anybody to reach counts against the number with no clicks, and gets named a stretch at a time.

items.lead: A stop inside a planned window never asks
items.text: Planned time stays planned, and the availability number is not punished for a wash.
Naming it turns it back into an unplanned stop and its time re-enters the number — a person's call, not a calendar's.

items.lead: The three doors from the list
items.text: The same three doors answer a stop later, from the list, when the answer did not come at the restart.

sections.title: Two honest OEEs, over the window you choose.
cols: One number cannot answer two fair questions, so the page prints both: what the machine could have made, and whether the jobs met the rate their own recipe promised. Everything on the page obeys one window, and the page opens on the window that has just finished.

sections.title: Quality, first pass
Quality counts the first pass, every time.

screen.chrome: EPS · Beverage Line 7 · the reject count
screen.caption: where the reject count came from, and whether it has been restated since

items.text: The count comes off the line's own counter, taken from the count point furthest down the flow.
The lab signs the verdict on the batch record; the signed count replaces the counter for that batch and the period redraws.

items.lead: A verdict after the shift closed
items.text: Sign it anyway: the period that made the product owns it, and wears a mark saying when, by whom, and from what to what.
Both figures side by side, so the gap closes itself instead of costing trust.
The page says what became of the rejects is not measured, rather than printing a zero.

items.lead: A unit put right stays a reject
items.text: First pass and every pass — so the figure cannot flatter the process it exists to expose.

items.lead: A verdict is added, never edited
items.text: An older signed count is superseded on the record and stays readable beside the one that replaced it, with who signed each and when.

screens.caption: where the verdict is signed: the batch record's two signatures, and the count quality signs against the machine's own

sections.title: Quality counts the first pass, every time.
cols: The reject count comes off the line's own counter until a person signs a different one, and then the signed count wins. A unit that had to be put right counts as a reject the first time, so the figure cannot flatter the process it exists to expose.
The period that made the product owns it, and wears a mark saying when, by whom, and from what to what.

A verdict is added, never edited: an older signed count is superseded on the record and stays readable beside the one that replaced it, with who signed each and when. A supervisor who saw the old figure on the wall can tap the mark and read both, so a restated shift costs nothing in trust. Nothing anybody wrote is ever quietly removed.

sections.title: The handover, one press
The handover, printed and signed in one press.

screen.chrome: Reports · Beverage Line 7 · the shift review
screen.caption: a review as SOP prints it: the document number, the fingerprint, and the line that says it is uncontrolled without a signature

items.lead: The handover on paper, in one press
items.text: The window you are reading becomes a document with a number, a seal and a place in the archive.
The page's own parts, bound to real tags: the two OEE tiles, the six bands, the hour grid, the loss ranking and the downtime table.
On the server, in the site's own clock, over exactly the window on the dial: a shift, a day, a month, one job, or two instants cut by hand.
Frozen on arrival, given a document number and a fingerprint. Press again and you have a second document beside the first, never a refresh.
By name and capacity, proved with the signer's own password, bound to the run's seal, never edited and never withdrawn.
On the plant's letterhead in three languages, e-mailed to the list, filed as a PDF, exported as a table.
0 report servers · 0 third-party licences · 0 seats to read: no reporting product, no rendering licence, no designer bought separately. It is inside the platform.
Where a job window makes the two disagree about what the rate is called, the paper is the one telling the truth.

screens.caption: one button on the dial, and the window you are reading becomes paper
the same record as it comes off the paper

screens.alt: the module's door and the shift report, on a phone
screens.caption: the module's one door, always in the top bar · the shift report, read off the phone at the line
a narrow screen keeps every number: the chips carry the period, the sheet carries the hours

items.text: The door, and the card at the restart: what is waiting rides on the chip in the top bar, and the answering card opens where he is standing, not where a desk is.
The sheet, worst first: the hours ranked by what they lost, and the shift report beside them. The handover is read off the phone, at the line.
The same shift report: the document the shift closed with, and a trend under it. The number reaches him before the meeting does.

sections.title: The handover, printed and signed in one press.
cols: The window you are reading prints through the same engine that prints your batch certificates. One press, and the shift is a document with a number, a seal and a place in the archive.
The paper is the same calculation as the screen, and where a job window makes the two disagree about what the rate is called, the paper is the one telling the truth.

The same application, sized for a hand: nothing to install, nothing licensed per screen, three languages including right-to-left Arabic. On a phone the module has one door, and it is always in the top bar.
On a narrow screen the bars are dropped and every number is kept, so nothing is hidden from the person who happens to be holding a phone.
